quote.text: Philosophy does not promise to secure anything external for man, otherwise it would be admitting something that lies beyond its proper subject-matter. For as the material of the carpenter is wood, and that of statuary bronze, so the subject-matter of the art of living is each person's own life.
quote.author: Epictetus
quote.aiInsight:
• Parenthood:
    • Embrace the idea that nurturing a child is akin to tending your own inner garden; focus on cultivating their character from within rather than promising external gains.
    • Recognize that parenting is an art of life where your guidance shapes a child's destiny—your influence is the wood from which their life is built, much like the material of the carpenter.
  • Leadership:
    • Understand that leadership is ultimately a personal art; your strength and integrity determine the quality of the team, just as a sculptor relies on the substance of bronze to create beauty.
    • Focus on self-improvement and internal virtues to inspire those around you—genuine leadership grows from the mastery of one’s own life rather than external rewards.
  • Product Management:
    • Apply the wisdom of self-reliance to your work: the success of a product lies in the careful, thoughtful stewardship of its life cycle, much like carving a masterpiece from raw material.
    • Concentrate on refining each element within your control, understanding that true progress is made by mastering internal processes and virtues rather than chasing external validations.
